outfits.name: 14-103 Twin Battery
outfits.description: For their super battleships, the Navarchs designed this huge-bore turret. Though the reload time leaves much to be desired, the huge shots deliver crushing damage over a broad area; each shell could level a medium-sized human warship.

outfits.name: 10-77 Twin Battery
outfits.description: This is the primary weapon for the Navarchs' large battleships: a twin-barreled, wide-bore cannon that's slow to aim and fire but deals impeccable damage once it connects. The significant firing forces produced by the weapon require a special armored hardpoint (a barbette) to be installed.

outfits.name: 7-62 Twin Battery
outfits.description: This weapon is a far smaller caliber than its bigger brother, but has a longer relative barrel length to compensate, allowing its projectiles to fly similar distances despite their lighter payload. Despite the major downsizing, this turret still produces enough force when firing to require a barbette.

outfits.name: 4-26 Dual Turret
outfits.description: The 4-26 is designed as a secondary turret for the Navarchs' large battleships, or a more primary role for their smaller ships. One turret is not particularly impressive by itself, but when equipped en masse, they can be effective at wearing down opponents at a fair distance.

outfits.name: 1-18 Anti-Fighter Rig
outfits.description: For anti-fighter roles, this tiny, snappy turret is the Navarchs' first choice. Small enough to be mounted on nearly anything and capable of a freakishly high rate of fire, this turret is designed for close-ranged anti-swarm combat, with a wild spray and considerable damage output.

outfits.name: 1-24 Anti-Fighter Array
outfits.description: Developed for the Regio-class carrier, this larger implementation of the 1-18 model autocannon is designed to saturate an area in anti-fighter fire. Improvements to the design also include greatly improved velocity, and subsequently, increased range.

outfits.name: THEL Node
outfits.description: The Navarchs have relatively little experience with beam technology compared to their tried and true "energy shell" designs. This prototypical weapon (dubbed the Tactical High Energy Laser) is their first such combat-practical design; a huge beam that carves through all but the thickest armor in its path, though compared to its projectile-based bretheren it suffers in the shield damage department. 	While the weapon doesn't produce nearly as much firing force as its projectile-based counterparts, the energy and cooling requirements means it still needs a barbette to be handled properly.

outfits.name: Shock Blaster Delta
outfits.description: Shock Blasters were designed as a method of building turrets that could provide effective damage at range without needing a barbette. The Shock Blaster Delta is the largest design that was successful in its goal: A rapid-fire, anti-area blaster that drains the electrical energy of struck ships, able to be mounted on any ship with the capacities to support it and capable of long-distance operations.

outfits.name: 5-36 Bombardier
outfits.description: Found aboard the newly developed Subformae, these modest cannons are capable of delivering significant anti-capital damage, with the sophisticated projectile shapes causing a small amount of damage to hull regardless of the target's shield state.

outfits.name: 3-22 Bombardier
outfits.description: A highly specialized cannon designed for fighter-to-capital warfare. Though slightly smaller caliber than its battleship-mounted cousins, the 3-22 Bombardier is outfitted with armor-piercing projectile forms that cause immense damage on impact at the cost of poor performance against crowds. 	To counteract the considerable hit force buildup that can accrue on a target under fire from a large swarm of Subvarietas, the Navarchs have designed this weapon to pull a target slightly closer to the ship, significantly reducing the likelihood a sortie of Subvarietas will be kited away from their support fleet.

outfits.name: 0.6-16 Autocannon
outfits.description: An autocannon designed for use aboard the Subvarietas fighter. Though its per-shot damage is notably unimpressive, it is capable of a blistering rate of fire with shells that have a deceptively wide danger area, making it excellent for interfighter combat.

outfits.name: "Povenant" Anti-Scuttle
outfits.description: Anti-Scuttles are area-of-effect devices that produce a powerful shield recovery effect during combat. Though even this small model of Anti-Scuttle requires a substantial amount of space and energy generation to operate, it is capable of recovering the shields of surrounding ships rather readily. Though the physical "ring" of influence highlights where the Anti-Scuttle is most effective, the rig's radius of effect caps out at about double what is observable to the naked eye. Because they operate on similar principles to Breach Sealant, Anti-Scuttles are also capable of repairing some of a ship's hull (though at a greatly diminished rate, and only within the visible ring).

outfits.name: Monolithic Anti-Missile
outfits.description: This Anti-Missile system is specially designed for carriers or other ships with few hardpoints, but otherwise large capacity for weapons. Though the Formidable Anti-Missile offers more balanced performance, the Monolithic model has supreme range, allowing it to cast a wide net of defense over an allied fleet.

outfits.name: Formidable Anti-Missile
outfits.description: The Formidable Anti-Missile is the standard-issue missile defense system for Navarch ships. Though it doesn't quite pack as much punch-per-ton as its smaller brother, it has greater range and higher per-shot power, massively increasing the likelihood a single shot will be needed to thwart a missile.

outfits.name: Intimidating Anti-Missile
outfits.description: Designed for light ships with a large amount of hardpoints, the Intimidating Anti-Missile is the smallest anti-missile system offered by the Navarchs. Its range is quite unimpressive compared to their larger anti-missile systems, but allows a ship to keep itself clear of enemy missile barrages.

outfits.name: Phase Torpedo
outfits.description: Named for their ability to move through space, air, or water, these heavy torpedoes consume massive amounts of energy and move slowly, but inflict devastating damage on hit, to the point where no shield can prevent at least some hull damage from leaking through.

outfits.name: Lathe Mine Bay
outfits.description: Lathe Mines are a particularly brutal type of obstacle that the Navarchs designed to be laid out in great numbers, dealing crushing damage to any ship who dares to stumble into them. Using similar technology to the phase torpedo, Lathe Mines cause heavy damage even through shields. The unique design of the Lathe mines means that, though they're intended as a trap, they are capable of serving as a form of anti-area projectile in the right conditions.

outfits.name: Ransacker ALS
outfits.description: Ransacker Missiles are a surprisingly unrefined weapon; easily replaceable missiles that split into a wide barrage of smaller explosives, pelting enemy fleets with an enormous amount of cluster munitions. 	Ransackers are launched at a reduced launch pressure, reducing load on the ship and allowing 9 to be launched from a relatively compact platform. However, the fact that the projectiles are assembled on the spot means reload time leaves something to be desired.

outfits.name: Hyperdrive Malformer
outfits.description: True to its name, this weapon works in a similar method to a commonplace hyperdrive; it uses a large quantity of deuterium to produce a large explosion. However, instead of tucking it into a safe region of spacetime to accelerate the ship, the device warps the explosion a good distance in front of the firing ship, causing a devastating explosion. According to Navarch legend, this was the weapon that caused the Drak and Quarg to seal the Navarchs away. 	Somehow, the Navarchs have found a way to program the explosion in a way that it doesn't harm allied ships, meaning that, for a weapon of mass destruction, it's surprisingly safe to use.

outfits.name: Unbound Gauss Slug
outfits.description: This three-ton hunk of yottrite alloy is ammunition for the Unbound Gauss Drive. The acceleration the slugs experience is intense enough to distend the slug over the course of firing, but the result is an unstoppable column of destruction that cuts through all in its path.

outfits.name: Unbound Gauss Drive
outfits.description: The earliest phases of this weapon's development harken back to before the Navarchs even first came into contact with the Quarg; an early attempt at using energy to replace the fuel in a Hyperdrive's operation, allowing a planet to theoretically launch fighters without any need for deuterium or worry of fallout from the fusion explosion that powers a Hyperdrive. The device failed, and was shelved for millenia. 	Relatively recently, however, some attention was brought back to the device, with the hopes that it could be turned into an effective weapon against swarms of Quarg Automata. The resultant weapon fires enormous yottrite-alloy slugs at near-light speed, causing an explosive effect on target and effortlessly cutting through all in its way. 	(Note: The amount of contact per shot can vary with enemy size, so damage per second is approximate.)

description.text: There doesn't seem to be anything here, save for a single tower with a small terminal.
Save for a single small tower with a terminal for interfacing, there doesn't seem to be anything here.
Save for a small tower with a terminal for basic operations, nothing is here.

Arragat Harbor acts largely as a reserve shipyard for its host planet, but also serves as the single largest outrigger interchange point for Navarch captains looking to adjust their fleets' capabilities before heading out on more missions. As such, it is quite busy here, despite the relative inelegance of Navarch stations compared to their terrestrial worlds.

spaceport.text: The station is almost entirely spaceport, with artificial gravity being the only thing from keeping cargo and personnel from tumbling off the platforms. Numerous small tug drones work to expediently guide interchanging outriggers between ships, and a few Navarchs can be seen taking pictures of the bright trails left behind by the small nanoplasma thrusters the tugs use.

description.text: This is one of the few worlds with enough notable landmass for the Navarchs to have built landbound ship facilities. Besides that, it is also a super-ocean world, with a surface area nearly 6 times larger than Earth, nearly 98% of which is water. As such, it serves as the perfect staging ground for the Navarchs' massive warfleets.

spaceport.text: The spaceport sprawls all over and around a lone continent around the size of south america; large ships wait at port around the coast, with several channels reserved for ships coming in for landing. Each dock here could hold 5-6 human ships of any size.

description.text: Chukchi was originally a military outpost, but has since been rebranded a large-scale fishing colony due to the presence of many species of hyper-productive fish; this one planet alone is capable of sustaining the food needs of nearly a fifth of the Navarchs' population.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is entirely seabound, with large "runways" for ships to land on the water. As expected, the scope is truly massive; each dock here is roughly six times the size of the largest human space docks.

description.text: Easibe is a very warm, prosperous ocean world, with large stakes in the industries of both farming and deep-sea drilling for oil.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is unremarkable by Navarch standards, though there is a surprisingly active tourism industry despite the Navarchs' lack of civilian ships.

description.text: Laptev is a temperate and calm, but otherwise boring ocean world; it is valued by the Navarchs only as a staging point for military fleets.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is almost comparable to a rural human spaceport, despite the size of the individual docks; parked vessels awaiting launches for patrols are a frequent sight, drifting idly through the mist.

description.text: Pechora is an ice world, but plays home to some crucial material refineries; as such, large channels of water have been carved out of the multiple-kilomter-thick ice sheets that evenly obscure the true surface of the planet, with small ships patrolling and using small heat rays to ensure the channels don't refreeze.

spaceport.text: The spaceport on Pechora is highly organized and automated; even the Navarchs' largest cargo ships are very swiftly loaded with kilotons of refined metals for export.

description.text: Fochexa is a warm ocean world with high, sharp spires of rock that stretch from the ocean floor to the surface, forming small islands anywhere from a few feet to a mile across. These landmasses aren't large enough to establish any sort of presence on, but they do lend the Navarchs a helping hand when it comes to monitoring the drifting of the spaceport.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is a sprawling complex of docks and channels, serving many military fleets as they pass through here. This planet serves as a critical chokepoint, and as such, is heavily guarded.

description.text: Beaufort is an artificial planet made from aeons of accumulated metal slag painstakingly melted together using its parent star's residual heat, before being poulated with large water channels to accomodate a limited Navarch presence here. Beaufort's value comes from the presence of yottrite in its home system, which the Navarchs use in their ships and weapons.

spaceport.text: Beaufort's spaceport seems to have been formed of molten metal slag like much of the rest of its surface, with natural outcrops serving as docking bays. Though the planet's surface is surprisingly temperate and has enough gravity to hold the water channels in place, it has no noticeable atmosphere.

description.text: Norvik is a large ocean world ripe with many rare and exotic metals, and is a critical mining planet for the Navarchs; however, twice an orbit, the moon "dips" in the rings of its parent planet, causing horrific meteor showers. As such, all ships staioned here are above a certain size, to avoid damage incurred by the showers.

spaceport.text: The spacport here consists only of large docks, and are heavily reinforced; in fact, you aren't walking along the metal structure at all, but instead shields over 2 feet thick. Meteoroids of various sizes are littered throughout the spaceport's scaffoldlike walkways, and there always seems to be some part under repair.

description.text: Beneath a thick layer of fog lies a planet with a vibrant rest-hued ocean, coloured so because of the absurdly high iron content of the water. Navarch ships here have to land with shields fully enabled to avoid iron particulate clinging to the exterior of their hulls. The iron here is, in fact, so infused into the water, that occasionally large enough storm clouds will have the mineral content necessary to rain iron as if it were clean water, requiring all of the ships and buildings here to run their shields all the time to avoid being petrified like the few small species of tree native to the islands.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is encased in a large, domular shield that protects it from the "rust rain". Despite this, there is a rather robust shipyard located here, taking advantage of the practically limitless sources of raw materials in the waters and small islands around the spaceport.

description.text: Leload Station is a mining platform that was built by the Navarchs to take advantage of the colossal amount of raw resources available in the system; as a consequence, however, Leiload System is the subject of frequent asteroid impacts, and thus heavy defenses are necessary; some of the turrets here are sourced from the research centers nearby, using the station as a testbed for long-ranged cannons and other such things.

spaceport.text: Unlike other Navarch Stations, there is a suprising amount of non-dock station here, with vast interior spaces used for mineral processing and storage. The working population here exceeds some human planets, with a few pamphlets boasting a figure of "800,000 strong arms in the workplace family".

description.text: Rugiboden is a large ocean planet with wild and unpredictable tides due to its 3 moons, one of which orbits "backwards" around the planet. Due to this, there's some research interest, and nanoplasma engines are often tested in the choppy waters.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is fairly small, hosted vertically along some large cliff faces, with docks that float somewhat freely on the water to avoid fighting the jostling tides. Fleet positions here are fairly uncommon, except for military contractors testing prototype works.

description.text: The Navarchs aren't much for luxurious living, instead preferring to show off their status with impressive private militias. However, Cantabri is one of the few worlds reserved for the elite who doesn't want to spend their whole life aboard a cruising vessel. The planet's seas are a rich blue, and are calm enough that you can see your reflection in them. The Navarchs here are a slightly uppity sort compared to most you've met, but the mood here is overall pleasant and tranquil.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is built in a specifically reserved sect of ocean, leaving the rest of the waters placid for the locals to enjoy. The market here deals in lots of luxury goods, and most Navarchs here seem to be of a significantly different caste than the hard-working naval crews or the diligent researchers, and most attempt to stop you to tell you stories of their "past lives" as one of such roles.

description.text: Byscay is an ocean world buried under thick fog. Apparently, it was one of the first worlds the Navarchs settled post-exile, contributing to why all Navarch ships have overly powerful two-way telemetry transmitters.

spaceport.text: Hidden in the fog is the spaceport, where conditions are nearly white-out. You can't comfortably see from one side of a dock to another, and it seems the locals don't fare much better, as powerful spotlights are a feature every few yards. The locals here all have loud conversations as they work, presumably to give eachother ample notice of their location.

description.text: A warm ocean planet tidally locked with its parent brown dwarf, Straido is home to a large maritime city that's responsible for exports of fish across a good swathe of Navarch space. The population here exceeds 100 billion individuals, and the planet is remarkably self-sufficient compared to similarly urban human worlds.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is designed mostly for cargo and logistical ships rather than warships, so capital warships are typically serviced by intraplanetary shuttlecraft that use the deck space on such warships as landing pads. Despite this, orders are conducted with surprising efficiency, with many ships hosting shuttles even before they've come to rest in the water.

description.text: A snow world, Blihano is valued for the pelts of its native creatures, which are used to make exotic textiles. Hunting here is carefully regulated to ensure the species here aren't overhunted. Despite this, it remains a popular sporting world, and a spaceport in a small, artificial ocean a few hundred miles in any direction serves most of the planet.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is confined to a small ocean kept artificially melted by ships with special heat rays. Small boats trawl the surface, blasting ice back into a liquid form. The residents here have many stories about ships being damaged by the ice refreezing.

description.text: Resei is a perplexing gas giant formed mostly of water over a much denser gas core. As such, it forms an ocean that's miles deep, but with essentially no bottom. As such, many Navarch researchers have been drawn to this world, leading to it becoming a very advanced world.

spaceport.text: The spaceport has two layers, one for above-water interactions typical of Navarch fleets, but a second, subaquatic layer make of what looks to be reinforced glass, serving submarine-like vehicles as they dive deep into the oceans to investigate the turbulent zones where water and the gas core mix.

description.text: Tyrrhen is a research world focused on developing post-scarcity sources of energy and materials. Rumour has it that, behind closed doors, there are prototype cells capable of scrubbing the cosmic microwave background for energy.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is fairly secluded, hosting a few small research fleets at a time. Contrary to most of Navarch space, where crews commonly sing shanties or converse while they work, the crews here are fairly quiet, keeping talk largely to just business.

description.text: Cagliari is a mining outpost that forgot to stop growing about a millenium ago. It is now one of the largest, most populous worlds in Navarch space, owing its prosperity to an absurdly high mineral content in the system it inhabits. Additionally, Cagliari supplies some exotic materials to research systems nearby, earning it a fair pay in the open market. It is for this reason that the Navarchs widely refer to this planet as their "home away from home", despite the fact that the planet doesn't even have a proper shipyard; just a basic station for supplying and outfitting logistical vessels.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is constructed around long fjords, where logistical ships can come to a low cruising speed and still be serviced by the time they reach the opening at the other end of the fjords the supply depots are built around. In this way, it is very rare that cargo jams happen, as ships are constantly on the move through well-organized supply lines.

description.text: Venetioon is a temperate ocean world, home to frequent rain, but very little storms. The water here is exceptionally soft, so many Navarchs come here for recreation. There's some industry here, but it's largely administrative and bureaucratic, leading to a surprisingly quiet world.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is fairly calm, though many Navarch tourists end up pulling you into photos, with or without your permission. The mood of the spaceport is jovial, with work crews loading at a very lax pace compared to more heavily regulated worlds.

description.text: Gunaple is a military-industrial world, home to large shipyards specializing in missile boat construction and the production of missile fabrication units for use aboard said missile boats.

spaceport.text: A fair amount of the docking space is reserved for newly built or still-building missile boats, with some docks open for pedestrian viewing. Navarchs of all ages can be seen admiring the thousands-strong work crews that work on putting ships together.

description.text: Uladant Station is a heavily fortified military-research station, where ships of all kinds are put to test against the abnormally strong Quarg Automaton presence in the system. Housing facilities are surprisingly common here, considering it's not often an hour goes by without the station being lurched around by the firing of a dozen or more gigantic gun batteries.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is heavily guarded by large turrets, similar to those aboard Navarch ships. Experimental missile launchers occasionally fire into open space, hoping to pre-emptively strike an encroaching Quarg target. Military fleets are far from short in supply here, with some of the highest Navarch presence in any system.

description.text: Porwant Station is one of the few places in Navarch space where the equipment for properly processing yottrite can be found, and the resultant resources produced are shipped to all corners of Navarch space.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is fairly sparse, and this is one of the stations incapable of interchanging outriggers. As such, save for small fleets coming to pick up allotments of yottrite-derived materials, the spaceport is rather quiet.

description.text: Venif is a super-ocean world, rich not in resources, but space and tranquil waters. Many industries, both labor and bureaucratic, have been set up here, and over the course of time the planet has become one of the few places where all the stars have aligned to allow for Supravitae construction.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is a marvel of automated engineering, with thousands of workers working smoothly with machines to assemble Supravitaes for use in Navarch warfleets. It is for this reason alone that Venif's spaceport is so huge; pristine Supravitaes lining the docks, awaiting their new captains and crews.

description.text: Seanor is an industrial powerhouse, responsible not for the export of ships and outfits, but many commodities needed by the Navarch population. The population here is nearly 500 billion, with much of the industry taking place in subaquatic sectors in the shallow end of the oceans, protecting from the scorching heat of the star the planet is tidally locked with.

spaceport.text: Seanor's spaceport is a ringworld-esque docking structure, constructed in the twilight zone between the sun-facing and dark sides of the planet. Though the spaceport isn't particularly special beyond this, the permanent sunset is breathtaking, and even the locals who've been here all their lives can be seen taking an appreciative glance every now and then.

description.text: Gulboth is a rocky world by Navarch standards, but is still about 70% ocean by surface area. Most of the land here is high continents, shattered with fjords. The native species here are mostly flighted creatures, the smallest of which is still about 5 feet tall when full grown. As such, hunting is a popular sport here.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is an interesting mix of highly advanced Navarch fare and rural, sporting community energy, with decorated admirals and rural sporting bumpkins jovially sharing the same streets and amenities on-world.

description.text: Shearish is a fairly backwater Navarch world, home to a few billion Navarch citizens. There's a limited research presence here, but overall the planet is widely considered of little importance to the Navarchs.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is built in the frigid, but unfrozen waters of the equator. Compared to some larger Navarch worlds, the pace here is rather laid back, and a significant portion of the working population seems to be retired volunteers.

description.text: Kotorbay is a large ocean world, home to one of the largest mineral processing and distributing centers in all of Navarch space. The minerals here supply many nearby shipyards, including those located on-world; however, very few military ships are constructed here.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is a highly optimized machine, rapidly loading vast quantities of minerals into any logistical ship that comes into port with reckless efficiency. It's operations like these that show how the Navarchs can so capably contend with the Quarg.

description.text: Secelt is a large, rocky ocean world, home to large peninsulas that house large factory complexes. A large logistics shipyard is set up here, allowing native captains to take jobs exporting the large amounts of refined and manufactured resources from here, but it is otherwise surprisingly underpopulated, with a permanent residence of only about 5 billion Navarchs.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is built around a large inlet in one of the larger continental shelves, where a luxuriant amount of loading equipment serves to load and unload large amounts of cargo from the frequent logistical fleets.

description.text: This world's water is largely in the form of large lakes, and thus the Navarch presence here is somewhat limited. However, it is a very productive farming world, producing feed for farm animals across a fair portion of Navarch space. Because of this, Iroise's limited shipyard space is reserved entirely for logistical ships.

spaceport.text: The spaceports are built across a few great lakes, most of which are only just deep enough for an Imperium to safely touch down in without major complications. As such the "diving lanes" are tightly regulated, ships being shuttled in and out of port very quickly to make the most of the limited deep water available.

description.text: Bayja is an ocean moon that exhibits extremely strong tidal actions due to the gravity of its host planet; the tides here can exceed a grade of 5 degrees during the "close" part of the planet's rotation. As such, permanent settlements are a rarity here, with most livingspaces just being retired military ships (some of which are old enough that they are no longer sold in Navarch space).

spaceport.text: The "spaceport" is essentially just a Supravitae that has had most of its weapons stripped off in favour of marketplaces and communications equipment, co-ordinating the thousands of independent houseboats on-world. Some free-floating raftlike boats exist to serve trade between fleets, driven by smaller versions of the nanoplasma engines used on ships.

description.text: Ulad Station started as a small research station for the sake of researching the vast wormhole network threaded through Navarch space, but has quickly grown to be a hub of Navarch research, with its Outrigger facilities being opened and a small shipyard being opened up to see how newly built prototype ships survive wormhole navigation.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is surprisingly robust, stretching a good distance around the wormhole. Outriggers and Experimental vessels compete somewhat for the slightly limited dock space, but overall, things seem to operate fairly smoothly.

description.text: Kvarken is a luscious tropical world, and is home to a thriving forestry industry. The Navarchs do not use much wood in their constructions, but it is valued for its carbon content, ease of transport, and renewability.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is a healthy mix of large-scale industry and small-scale independent hobby shops; some Navarchs enjoy hunting the exotic and often dangerous wildlife here, and several market stall owners offer you a chance to try exotic meat and fish prepared in equally exotic ways.

description.text: Vainas is a small shipping world, often acting as a reserve for supplies either exported from or needed on Kvarken. As such, the planet is generally quiet, and hosts a modest population of around ten billion Navarchs.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is fairly small and lax, at least by Navarch standards; ships still regularly land and take off, but it's rare that any of the largest Navarch ships end up here for long.

description.text: Curoni is one of the few planets that hosts outrigger exhcanges, featuring a vast array of lifts and chambers to rapidly cycle through existing stock.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is a fairly active place, hosting a healthy mix of backline vessels; mostly outriggers, but many missile boats as well. Some Navarchs are even making deals to exchange ships.

description.text: There doesn't seem to be anything here, save for a single tower with a small terminal.
Save for a small tower with a terminal for basic operations, nothing is here.
Save for a single small tower with a terminal for interfacing, there doesn't seem to be anything here.

This is one of the few worlds with enough notable landmass for the Navarchs to have built landbound ship facilities. Besides that, it is also a super-ocean world, with a surface area nearly 6 times larger than Earth, nearly 98% of which is water. As such, it serves as the perfect staging ground for the Navarchs' massive warfleets.

spaceport.text: The spaceport sprawls all over and around a lone continent around the size of south america; large ships wait at port around the coast, with several channels reserved for ships coming in for landing. Each dock here could hold 5-6 human ships of any size.

description.text: Arragat Harbor acts largely as a reserve shipyard for its host planet, but also serves as the single largest outrigger interchange point for Navarch captains looking to adjust their fleets' capabilities before heading out on more missions. As such, it is quite busy here, despite the relative inelegance of Navarch stations compared to their terrestrial worlds.

spaceport.text: The station is almost entirely spaceport, with artificial gravity being the only thing from keeping cargo and personnel from tumbling off the platforms. Numerous small tug drones work to expediently guide interchanging outriggers between ships, and a few Navarchs can be seen taking pictures of the bright trails left behind by the small nanoplasma thrusters the tugs use.

description.text: Chukchi was originally a military outpost, but has since been rebranded a large-scale fishing colony due to the presence of many species of hyper-productive fish; this one planet alone is capable of sustaining the food needs of nearly a fifth of the Navarchs' population.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is entirely seabound, with large "runways" for ships to land on the water. As expected, the scope is truly massive; each dock here is roughly six times the size of the largest human space docks.

description.text: Easibe is a very warm, prosperous ocean world, with large stakes in the industries of both farming and deep-sea drilling for oil.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is unremarkable by Navarch standards, though there is a surprisingly active tourism industry despite the Navarchs' lack of civilian ships.

description.text: Laptev is a temperate and calm, but otherwise boring ocean world; it is valued by the Navarchs only as a staging point for military fleets.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is almost comparable to a rural human spaceport, despite the size of the individual docks; parked vessels awaiting launches for patrols are a frequent sight, drifting idly through the mist.

description.text: Pechora is an ice world, but plays home to some crucial material refineries; as such, large channels of water have been carved out of the multiple-kilomter-thick ice sheets that evenly obscure the true surface of the planet, with small ships patrolling and using small heat rays to ensure the channels don't refreeze.

spaceport.text: The spaceport on Pechora is highly organized and automated; even the Navarchs' largest cargo ships are very swiftly loaded with kilotons of refined metals for export.

description.text: Beaufort is an artificial planet made from aeons of accumulated metal slag painstakingly melted together using its parent star's residual heat, before being poulated with large water channels to accomodate a limited Navarch presence here. Beaufort's value comes from the presence of yottrite in its home system, which the Navarchs use in their ships and weapons.

spaceport.text: Beaufort's spaceport seems to have been formed of molten metal slag like much of the rest of its surface, with natural outcrops serving as docking bays. Though the planet's surface is surprisingly temperate and has enough gravity to hold the water channels in place, it has no noticeable atmosphere.

description.text: Fochexa is a warm ocean world with high, sharp spires of rock that stretch from the ocean floor to the surface, forming small islands anywhere from a few feet to a mile across. These landmasses aren't large enough to establish any sort of presence on, but they do lend the Navarchs a helping hand when it comes to monitoring the drifting of the spaceport.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is a sprawling complex of docks and channels, serving many military fleets as they pass through here. This planet serves as a critical chokepoint, and as such, is heavily guarded.

description.text: Norvik is a large ocean world ripe with many rare and exotic metals, and is a critical mining planet for the Navarchs; however, twice an orbit, the moon "dips" in the rings of its parent planet, causing horrific meteor showers. As such, all ships staioned here are above a certain size, to avoid damage incurred by the showers.

spaceport.text: The spacport here consists only of large docks, and are heavily reinforced; in fact, you aren't walking along the metal structure at all, but instead shields over 2 feet thick. Meteoroids of various sizes are littered throughout the spaceport's scaffoldlike walkways, and there always seems to be some part under repair.

description.text: Beneath a thick layer of fog lies a planet with a vibrant rest-hued ocean, coloured so because of the absurdly high iron content of the water. Navarch ships here have to land with shields fully enabled to avoid iron particulate clinging to the exterior of their hulls. The iron here is, in fact, so infused into the water, that occasionally large enough storm clouds will have the mineral content necessary to rain iron as if it were clean water, requiring all of the ships and buildings here to run their shields all the time to avoid being petrified like the few small species of tree native to the islands.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is encased in a large, domular shield that protects it from the "rust rain". Despite this, there is a rather robust shipyard located here, taking advantage of the practically limitless sources of raw materials in the waters and small islands around the spaceport.

description.text: Resei is a perplexing gas giant formed mostly of water over a much denser gas core. As such, it forms an ocean that's miles deep, but with essentially no bottom. As such, many Navarch researchers have been drawn to this world, leading to it becoming a very advanced world.

spaceport.text: The spaceport has two layers, one for above-water interactions typical of Navarch fleets, but a second, subaquatic layer make of what looks to be reinforced glass, serving submarine-like vehicles as they dive deep into the oceans to investigate the turbulent zones where water and the gas core mix.

description.text: Leload Station is a mining platform that was built by the Navarchs to take advantage of the colossal amount of raw resources available in the system; as a consequence, however, Leiload System is the subject of frequent asteroid impacts, and thus heavy defenses are necessary; some of the turrets here are sourced from the research centers nearby, using the station as a testbed for long-ranged cannons and other such things.

spaceport.text: Unlike other Navarch Stations, there is a suprising amount of non-dock station here, with vast interior spaces used for mineral processing and storage. The working population here exceeds some human planets, with a few pamphlets boasting a figure of "800,000 strong arms in the workplace family".

description.text: A warm ocean planet tidally locked with its parent brown dwarf, Straido is home to a large maritime city that's responsible for exports of fish across a good swathe of Navarch space. The population here exceeds 100 billion individuals, and the planet is remarkably self-sufficient compared to similarly urban human worlds.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is designed mostly for cargo and logistical ships rather than warships, so capital warships are typically serviced by intraplanetary shuttlecraft that use the deck space on such warships as landing pads. Despite this, orders are conducted with surprising efficiency, with many ships hosting shuttles even before they've come to rest in the water.

description.text: Rugiboden is a large ocean planet with wild and unpredictable tides due to its 3 moons, one of which orbits "backwards" around the planet. Due to this, there's some research interest, and nanoplasma engines are often tested in the choppy waters.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is fairly small, hosted vertically along some large cliff faces, with docks that float somewhat freely on the water to avoid fighting the jostling tides. Fleet positions here are fairly uncommon, except for military contractors testing prototype works.

description.text: A snow world, Blihano is valued for the pelts of its native creatures, which are used to make exotic textiles. Hunting here is carefully regulated to ensure the species here aren't overhunted. Despite this, it remains a popular sporting world, and a spaceport in a small, artificial ocean a few hundred miles in any direction serves most of the planet.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is confined to a small ocean kept artificially melted by ships with special heat rays. Small boats trawl the surface, blasting ice back into a liquid form. The residents here have many stories about ships being damaged by the ice refreezing.

description.text: Byscay is an ocean world buried under thick fog. Apparently, it was one of the first worlds the Navarchs settled post-exile, contributing to why all Navarch ships have overly powerful two-way telemetry transmitters.

spaceport.text: Hidden in the fog is the spaceport, where conditions are nearly white-out. You can't comfortably see from one side of a dock to another, and it seems the locals don't fare much better, as powerful spotlights are a feature every few yards. The locals here all have loud conversations as they work, presumably to give eachother ample notice of their location.

description.text: The Navarchs aren't much for luxurious living, instead preferring to show off their status with impressive private militias. However, Cantabri is one of the few worlds reserved for the elite who doesn't want to spend their whole life aboard a cruising vessel. The planet's seas are a rich blue, and are calm enough that you can see your reflection in them. The Navarchs here are a slightly uppity sort compared to most you've met, but the mood here is overall pleasant and tranquil.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is built in a specifically reserved sect of ocean, leaving the rest of the waters placid for the locals to enjoy. The market here deals in lots of luxury goods, and most Navarchs here seem to be of a significantly different caste than the hard-working naval crews or the diligent researchers, and most attempt to stop you to tell you stories of their "past lives" as one of such roles.

description.text: Bayja is an ocean moon that exhibits extremely strong tidal actions due to the gravity of its host planet; the tides here can exceed a grade of 5 degrees during the "close" part of the planet's rotation. As such, permanent settlements are a rarity here, with most livingspaces just being retired military ships (some of which are old enough that they are no longer sold in Navarch space).

spaceport.text: The "spaceport" is essentially just a Supravitae that has had most of its weapons stripped off in favour of marketplaces and communications equipment, co-ordinating the thousands of independent houseboats on-world. Some free-floating raftlike boats exist to serve trade between fleets, driven by smaller versions of the nanoplasma engines used on ships.

description.text: Ulad Station started as a small research station for the sake of researching the vast wormhole network threaded through Navarch space, but has quickly grown to be a hub of Navarch research, with its Outrigger facilities being opened and a small shipyard being opened up to see how newly built prototype ships survive wormhole navigation.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is surprisingly robust, stretching a good distance around the wormhole. Outriggers and Experimental vessels compete somewhat for the slightly limited dock space, but overall, things seem to operate fairly smoothly.

description.text: Seanor is an industrial powerhouse, responsible not for the export of ships and outfits, but many commodities needed by the Navarch population. The population here is nearly 500 billion, with much of the industry taking place in subaquatic sectors in the shallow end of the oceans, protecting from the scorching heat of the star the planet is tidally locked with.

spaceport.text: Seanor's spaceport is a ringworld-esque docking structure, constructed in the twilight zone between the sun-facing and dark sides of the planet. Though the spaceport isn't particularly special beyond this, the permanent sunset is breathtaking, and even the locals who've been here all their lives can be seen taking an appreciative glance every now and then.

description.text: Gulboth is a rocky world by Navarch standards, but is still about 70% ocean by surface area. Most of the land here is high continents, shattered with fjords. The native species here are mostly flighted creatures, the smallest of which is still about 5 feet tall when full grown. As such, hunting is a popular sport here.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is an interesting mix of highly advanced Navarch fare and rural, sporting community energy, with decorated admirals and rural sporting bumpkins jovially sharing the same streets and amenities on-world.

description.text: This world's water is largely in the form of large lakes, and thus the Navarch presence here is somewhat limited. However, it is a very productive farming world, producing feed for farm animals across a fair portion of Navarch space. Because of this, Iroise's limited shipyard space is reserved entirely for logistical ships.

spaceport.text: The spaceports are built across a few great lakes, most of which are only just deep enough for an Imperium to safely touch down in without major complications. As such the "diving lanes" are tightly regulated, ships being shuttled in and out of port very quickly to make the most of the limited deep water available.

description.text: Shearish is a fairly backwater Navarch world, home to a few billion Navarch citizens. There's a limited research presence here, but overall the planet is widely considered of little importance to the Navarchs.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is built in the frigid, but unfrozen waters of the equator. Compared to some larger Navarch worlds, the pace here is rather laid back, and a significant portion of the working population seems to be retired volunteers.

description.text: Secelt is a large, rocky ocean world, home to large peninsulas that house large factory complexes. A large logistics shipyard is set up here, allowing native captains to take jobs exporting the large amounts of refined and manufactured resources from here, but it is otherwise surprisingly underpopulated, with a permanent residence of only about 5 billion Navarchs.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is built around a large inlet in one of the larger continental shelves, where a luxuriant amount of loading equipment serves to load and unload large amounts of cargo from the frequent logistical fleets.

description.text: Gunaple is a military-industrial world, home to large shipyards specializing in missile boat construction and the production of missile fabrication units for use aboard said missile boats.

spaceport.text: A fair amount of the docking space is reserved for newly built or still-building missile boats, with some docks open for pedestrian viewing. Navarchs of all ages can be seen admiring the thousands-strong work crews that work on putting ships together.

description.text: Uladant Station is a heavily fortified military-research station, where ships of all kinds are put to test against the abnormally strong Quarg Automaton presence in the system. Housing facilities are surprisingly common here, considering it's not often an hour goes by without the station being lurched around by the firing of a dozen or more gigantic gun batteries.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is heavily guarded by large turrets, similar to those aboard Navarch ships. Experimental missile launchers occasionally fire into open space, hoping to pre-emptively strike an encroaching Quarg target. Military fleets are far from short in supply here, with some of the highest Navarch presence in any system.

description.text: Kotorbay is a large ocean world, home to one of the largest mineral processing and distributing centers in all of Navarch space. The minerals here supply many nearby shipyards, including those located on-world; however, very few military ships are constructed here.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is a highly optimized machine, rapidly loading vast quantities of minerals into any logistical ship that comes into port with reckless efficiency. It's operations like these that show how the Navarchs can so capably contend with the Quarg.

description.text: Cagliari is a mining outpost that forgot to stop growing about a millenium ago. It is now one of the largest, most populous worlds in Navarch space, owing its prosperity to an absurdly high mineral content in the system it inhabits. Additionally, Cagliari supplies some exotic materials to research systems nearby, earning it a fair pay in the open market. It is for this reason that the Navarchs widely refer to this planet as their "home away from home", despite the fact that the planet doesn't even have a proper shipyard; just a basic station for supplying and outfitting logistical vessels.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is constructed around long fjords, where logistical ships can come to a low cruising speed and still be serviced by the time they reach the opening at the other end of the fjords the supply depots are built around. In this way, it is very rare that cargo jams happen, as ships are constantly on the move through well-organized supply lines.

description.text: Tyrrhen is a research world focused on developing post-scarcity sources of energy and materials. Rumour has it that, behind closed doors, there are prototype cells capable of scrubbing the cosmic microwave background for energy.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is fairly secluded, hosting a few small research fleets at a time. Contrary to most of Navarch space, where crews commonly sing shanties or converse while they work, the crews here are fairly quiet, keeping talk largely to just business.

description.text: Venetioon is a temperate ocean world, home to frequent rain, but very little storms. The water here is exceptionally soft, so many Navarchs come here for recreation. There's some industry here, but it's largely administrative and bureaucratic, leading to a surprisingly quiet world.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is fairly calm, though many Navarch tourists end up pulling you into photos, with or without your permission. The mood of the spaceport is jovial, with work crews loading at a very lax pace compared to more heavily regulated worlds.

description.text: Porwant Station is one of the few places in Navarch space where the equipment for properly processing yottrite can be found, and the resultant resources produced are shipped to all corners of Navarch space.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is fairly sparse, and this is one of the stations incapable of interchanging outriggers. As such, save for small fleets coming to pick up allotments of yottrite-derived materials, the spaceport is rather quiet.

description.text: Venif is a super-ocean world, rich not in resources, but space and tranquil waters. Many industries, both labor and bureaucratic, have been set up here, and over the course of time the planet has become one of the few places where all the stars have aligned to allow for Supravitae construction.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is a marvel of automated engineering, with thousands of workers working smoothly with machines to assemble Supravitaes for use in Navarch warfleets. It is for this reason alone that Venif's spaceport is so huge; pristine Supravitaes lining the docks, awaiting their new captains and crews.

spaceport.text: The spaceport here is a healthy mix of large-scale industry and small-scale independent hobby shops; some Navarchs enjoy hunting the exotic and often dangerous wildlife here, and several market stall owners offer you a chance to try exotic meat and fish prepared in equally exotic ways.
